title: Efficiency ratios
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No existing point covers efficiency ratios such as the expense ratio or accounts receivable turnover; the closest, profit and monitoring performance, are related but different ideas.

draft.title: Efficiency ratios
card: Efficiency ratios show how well a business manages its costs and its money owed. A business that is efficient gets more from what it spends and collects.
expenses ÷ sales × 100. It shows costs as a share of sales. A lower ratio means the business spends less to earn each dollar of sales.
sales on credit ÷ accounts receivable. Accounts receivable is money owed to the business by customers. A higher turnover means customers pay more quickly.
Slow payment ties up cash the business needs for its own bills. A falling expense ratio or a rising turnover points to better efficiency.
draft.remember: Expense ratio: costs per dollar of sales. Receivable turnover: how fast customers pay.

a.q: A business's expense ratio falls from 40% to 35%. What does this show?
opts: Costs are a smaller share of its sales
Costs are a larger share of its sales
a.why: The expense ratio compares expenses with sales. A fall from 40% to 35% means each dollar of sales now carries less cost. It says nothing about how fast customers pay, which is the job of receivable turnover.
a.clue: The expense ratio compares costs with sales.

b.q: Priya's hardware store in Bathurst sells on credit. Its accounts receivable turnover drops from 12 to 8 over a year. What is the most likely meaning?
opts: Customers are taking longer to pay their accounts
Customers are paying their accounts more quickly
Costs have risen as a share of the store's sales
Costs have fallen as a share of the store's sales
b.why: Turnover shows how quickly customers pay, and a lower figure means slower payment. This leaves less cash for the store's own bills. Costs as a share of sales are measured by the expense ratio, not by this ratio.
b.clue: Ask which ratio measures customer payment speed, and which way it moved.

a.best: Costs are a smaller share of its sales

b.best: Customers are taking longer to pay their accounts
